edges.effect_quant: Adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor therapy consistently lowers bone mineral density relative to more bone-protective endocrine strategies, and the signal is strong enough that many trials focus on how to blunt the loss rather than whether it exists.
edges.population: women receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy for breast cancer, especially postmenopausal women
edges.mechanism: Aromatase inhibitors sharply reduce peripheral estrogen production. Because estrogen restrains osteoclast activity and supports bone remodeling balance, that endocrine shift accelerates bone turnover and drives net skeletal loss.
edges.summary: The most defensible conclusion is that aromatase inhibitors reduce bone mineral density and worsen bone safety compared with more estrogenic comparators such as tamoxifen. Randomized endocrine-therapy studies and later comparative meta-analysis all point the same way, which is why bone-protection strategies are routinely paired with these drugs in higher-risk patients.
edges.caveats: The absolute bone loss depends on menopausal status, baseline skeletal health, and whether bisphosphonates or denosumab are used alongside treatment. This edge captures the adverse skeletal direction of the endocrine exposure itself, not the residual risk after optimal bone-protective management.

evidence.citation: BrufskyA et al 2007 J Clin Oncol
evidence.notes: Zoledronic acid inhibits adjuvant letrozole-induced bone loss in postmenopausal women with early breast cancer.

effect_quant.comparator: lumbar-spine bone mineral density difference at 12 months between upfront and delayed zoledronic acid in women receiving letrozole

evidence.citation: GnantMF et al 2007 J Clin Oncol
evidence.notes: Zoledronic acid prevents cancer treatment-induced bone loss in premenopausal women receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy for hormone-responsive breast cancer: a report from the Austrian Breast and Colorectal Cancer Study Group.

effect_quant.comparator: bone mineral density change after 36 months in the anastrozole plus goserelin group without zoledronic acid

evidence.notes: Bone Safety Profile of Steroidal Aromatase Inhibitor in Comparison to Nonsteroidal Aromatase Inhibitors in Postmenopausal Women with Breast Cancer: A Network Meta-Analysis.
